title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the Order Book — Marine Defence, Data Centers & Emerging Bets

epigraph.quote: An order book is only as good as the engineering complexity inside it and the cash-collection terms attached to each milestone.
epigraph.author: Project Finance Maxim

web_blocks.html: Marine Electricals builds electrical automation, power-distribution, and marine-comms systems [2, 7]. It runs two core engines: Marine & Defence and Industry (led by Data Centres) [2, 7]. Smaller bets include EV charging, solar, and maritime software [2, 7]. Though rooted in naval work, the order book has flipped [7]. On September 30, 2026, Industrial and Data Centre orders hit ₹3,065 crore, or 87.2% of the ₹3,514 crore backlog [7]. Marine & Defence held ₹449 crore, or 12.8% [7].

Revenue growth mirrors that gap in execution speed [7]. In H1 FY27, consolidated sales rose 71% YoY to ₹664 crore [7]. The Industry segment surged 123% YoY in H1 FY27 and 164% YoY in Q2 FY27 on data center, chip, and plant deliveries [7]. Over the same span, Marine & Defence grew a steady 21% YoY in H1 FY27 (16% YoY in Q2 FY27) on naval fleet schedules [7].

web_blocks.takeaway: Data center and industrial power infrastructure now drive 87.2% of the ₹3,514 Cr backlog and +123% H1 FY27 segment growth, transforming Marine Electricals from a pure marine contractor into a digital-infrastructure power integrator [7].

web_blocks.html: Segment 1 Example — Indian Navy Stealth Frigate Package: Consider Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) or Mazagon Dock building a stealth frigate for the Indian Navy [2, 11]. Warships face underwater shock, constant vibration, salt spray, and heavy radar loads [2]. One switchboard arc fault can knock out propulsion or combat gear [2]. Marine Electricals acts as a pre-qualified Tier-1 integrator [2, 9]. Its Mumbai and Goa teams build shock-qualified main switchboards, emergency panels, and platform-control consoles [2, 9]. Naval inspectors witness Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT) before onboard fitment over 12 to 36 months [2, 9]. Tenders pay by milestones tied to delivery, fitment, and sea trials [1, 7]. High entry barriers give the firm ~50% domestic share in niche naval electricals [1, 7].

Segment 2 Example — Hyperscale Data Center Power Train Unit (PTU): Now look at a colocation developer like Princeton Digital Group (PDG) or STT Global Data Centres building a 50 MW hall in Navi Mumbai or Chennai [11]. For these operators, time-to-power is the main financial risk. Every week of delay costs high-margin cloud lease revenue. Site-built electrical rooms take months of sequential civil, cabling, and test work. Marine Electricals speeds this up by building a factory-tested Power Train Unit (PTU) at its 160,000 sq. ft. Loutulim, Goa plant [9]. Each unit pairs licensed Schneider Electric BlokSeT gear or ASTA-tested MEcubE+ panels with transformers, UPS links, busducts, and sensors [9, 10]. Teams test the skid in Goa, truck it to the site, and crane it onto its pad for fast commissioning [9, 10]. Delivery cycles shrink to 6–12 months, driving rapid sales growth [1, 17]. Still, bidding against global OEMs and local panel peers keeps operating margins at 10–12% [1, 17].

Segment 3 Example — Municipal EV Charging & Port VTMS: Through unit Evigo Charge Private Limited, the firm runs turnkey PPP EV charging rollouts, including revenue-share deals with Pune Municipal Corporation [12]. Evigo supplies 3.3 kW AC to 240 kW DC chargers, installs grid-tie panels, and manages billing on its Bijlify cloud app [12]. Separately, Canadian investee Xanatos Marine Ltd. transfers tech for TITAN Sentinel and TITAN Avips Vessel Traffic Management Systems (VTMS) [13]. These systems fuse radar, AIS, and coastal sensors for port authorities [13]. Both verticals remain small today, and Evigo relies on parent guarantees as station use scales [4].

Overseas units add niche reach without dominating group sales yet [4, 14]. In the UAE, MEL Power Systems FZC supplies marine switchboards and shore power for Gulf fleets [4]. In Italy, STI S.r.l. handles marine automation retrofits and renewable electricals [14]. Together, they give global shipping and data-center clients multi-region service support [2, 4]. Across both domestic and export markets, project mix shapes quarterly revenue swings [1, 7]. Marine deliveries depend on multi-year shipyard hull progress and defence inspection gates [2, 7]. Data-center PTU orders convert to revenue much faster once Goa factory slots and site pads are ready [7, 9]. Tracking that mix helps investors separate steady naval base load from faster hyperscaler capex waves [1, 7].

web_blocks.title: Mix-Shift Trade-Off: Velocity vs. Proprietary IP
paragraphs: Data center PTUs drive fast top-line growth (H1 FY27 Industry sales +123% YoY) and turn over in 6–12 months versus multi-year naval hulls [7].

Because PTUs use third-party breakers, transformers, and licensed BlokSeT frames, raw materials took 70.6% of FY26 sales (₹619 Cr on ₹877 Cr) [15]. Holding double-digit EBITDA margins requires high Goa plant use and tight contract pricing [15].

book_paragraphs: If you only glanced at the company's name, you would assume Marine Electricals makes its living exclusively on the water. That used to be true, and the marine heritage still anchors its engineering reputation. Today, however, the real engine of the business sits inside windowless, air-conditioned server halls.

By September 30, 2026, Marine Electricals' unexecuted order book had surged to 3,514 crore rupees. Break that backlog apart and you see a striking structural inversion: 3,065 crore rupees—more than 87 percent of the entire pipeline—came from the Industry and Data Centre segment, while Marine and Defence accounted for 449 crore rupees. In the first half of FY27 alone, industrial revenue jumped 123 percent year-on-year, and 164 percent in the second quarter, compared with a steady 21 percent rise in marine.

To understand how one engineering company can serve both an Indian Navy warship and a cloud hyperscaler, walk through two concrete projects from start to finish. First, imagine a stealth frigate taking shape at Mazagon Dock or Garden Reach Shipbuilders. On a combat vessel, a single electrical arc fault during rough seas or weapons firing can blind radar or disable propulsion. Marine Electricals designs shock-qualified, vibration-tested main and emergency switchboards alongside integrated platform-management consoles, puts them through grueling naval factory acceptance tests overseen by defence inspectors, and commissions them across a 12-to-36-month shipbuilding schedule. That work carries deep qualification moats and roughly 50 percent domestic share in specialized naval electrical niches—but it moves at the deliberate pace of defence procurement.

Now step onto a hyperscale data center campus in Navi Mumbai or Chennai for a client like Princeton Digital Group or STT Global Data Centres. Here, the customer's mortal enemy is time. Colocation operators lose substantial lease revenue for every week a data hall sits unpowered. Instead of assembling loose switchgear on a dusty construction site, Marine Electricals builds integrated Power Train Units—essentially pre-engineered, factory-tested electrical rooms packing medium-voltage and low-voltage switchgear, busducts, transformers, and power distribution units—inside its 160,000 square foot Goa facility. Those modular blocks are tested before leaving the factory floor, trucked to the site, and craned into place, shaving months off construction schedules.

Around these two core engines sit smaller, option-value bets. Subsidiary Evigo Charge builds public and fleet EV charging networks under the Bijlify software platform, including municipal revenue-sharing contracts such as Pune Municipal Corporation, deploying chargers ranging from 3.3 kilowatts to 240 kilowatts. Meanwhile, Canadian tie-up Xanatos Marine and associate Marks Marine Radio extend the maritime electronics suite into vessel-traffic radar software and marine radio communications. Both verticals are still in incubation, with Evigo leaning on parent corporate guarantees as it builds utilization. International arms in the UAE and Italy add regional marine and automation service reach.

The analytical tension in this mix shift is straightforward. Data center power trains give Marine Electricals extraordinary revenue velocity, turning over in 6 to 12 months rather than three years. Yet they are assembly-heavy: raw materials ate roughly 70.6 percent of FY26 sales. As the business shifts from bespoke naval panels toward high-volume data center skids, your job as an analyst is to watch whether operating scale in Goa keeps margins above 11 percent—or whether component pass-through and customer bargaining power cap profitability.

book_callouts.title: Follow the Backlog
book_callouts.text: When 87 percent of an order book sits in a single booming vertical—hyperscale data centers—execution speed soars, but so does sensitivity to hyperscaler capital-expenditure cycles.

book_subsections.title: Inside the Shipyard and the Hyperscale Data Hall
paragraphs: Let's step onto the shop floor to see what Marine Electricals actually builds in its two core verticals. In the Marine and Defence segment — which historically anchored the company and now represents roughly 12.8% of the ₹3,514 Cr September 2026 order book while growing +21% YoY in H1 FY27 — imagine an Indian Navy frigate under construction at Mazagon Dock in Mumbai. That vessel needs an integrated power management system that takes generation from diesel-alternators or gas turbines, distributes medium- and low-voltage power safely across weapon, radar, and propulsion loads, and automatically isolates faults if a compartment is damaged.

Marine Electricals engineers, integrates, and commissions those custom switchboards, integrated bridge systems, and automation consoles. Each shipset is bespoke, engineered to naval shock-grade specifications, and priced on multi-crore milestone contracts that can span two to four years from design freeze to sea trials.

Now contrast that with the Industry and Data Center segment, which accounts for 87.2% of the ₹3,514 Cr backlog and surged +123% YoY in H1 FY27. Picture a hyperscale data-center campus in Navi Mumbai or Chennai built by Princeton Digital Group, STT GDC, CtrlS, or Web Werks. A 30 MW AI-ready data hall cannot afford a single millisecond of power interruption, nor can the developer wait 18 months for brick-and-mortar electrical rooms to be wired on-site. Marine Electricals solves this by fabricating containerized Power Train Units (PTUs) in Goa — pre-integrated, factory-tested skids housing MV/LV switchgear (often built under its Schneider Electric BlokSeT license or ASTA-certified MEcubE+ architecture), busducts, UPS interfaces, and SCADA monitoring — shipped ready to plug into the data hall.

book_subsections.title: Revenue Mix, Margin Contrast & Why Data Centers Changed the Profile
paragraphs: Why does the mix shift between Marine/Defence and Industry/Data Centers matter so much to earnings quality? In H1 FY27, consolidated revenue rose 71% year-on-year to ₹664 Cr, but the two engines moved at very different speeds: Industry & Data Centers surged +123% YoY and now accounts for 87.2% of the ₹3,514 Cr open order book, while Marine grew a steadier +21% YoY and represents 12.8% of the backlog.

On the surface, data-center Power Train Units offer faster factory throughput than multi-year warship builds. Instead of waiting four years for a naval hull to be launched and commissioned, a containerized PTU built in Goa can be fabricated, factory-acceptance-tested, and dispatched within months. That faster cycle helped lift quarterly operating margins from 8%–9% in FY22–FY25 to 11% in FY26 and 12% in Q2 FY27. Yet the underlying commercial reality remains: whether building a naval main switchboard or a data-center PTU, Marine Electricals is assembling bought-out circuit breakers, relays, and transformers into engineered enclosures — meaning gross margins stay anchored near 29%–30%.

book_subsections.title: Evigo Charge & Adjacent Bets: Optionality vs. Core Focus
paragraphs: Beyond its two core engines of Naval/Marine and Data Center/Industry electricals, Marine Electricals also operates an EV-charging infrastructure arm through Evigo Charge Pvt. Ltd. and its Bijlify brand, supplying AC and DC fast chargers to fleet and commercial operators. While EV charging provides long-term thematic optionality, investors should keep its current financial materiality in perspective: the ₹3,514 Cr September 2026 order book is overwhelmingly driven by the 87.2% Industry/Data Center vertical and the 12.8% Marine vertical.

In our underwriting, we treat Evigo Charge, STI S.r.l. (Italy), and Xanatos Marine (Canada) as useful capability extensions rather than standalone valuation drivers. What moves the needle over the next three years is whether the Goa facility can convert its ₹3,514 Cr backlog into billed, collected cash.
